fieldValues.title: A Container is stored as a directory of one-line entry files, so concurrent membership edits merge per entry
fieldValues.decision_rationale: Under RFC-043 [R14] two branches that each add a member merge cleanly, but git merges the container file line by line and both appends collide at the end of one array. Measured over all four first-party corpora since 2026-08-21, 172 of 190 member edits were appends and 13 merges conflicted on a container file. RFC-038 ruled for elimination in storage over mitigation in tools; this applies that ruling to the last shared array, before the Continuity flip (axis 2-8) makes the layout permanent. One-line files make every rename-paired merge a visible conflict rather than a silent misapplied edit.
fieldValues.decision_statement: At dataModelRevision 11 every Container is stored as a directory: a one-line head carrying its own fields, and one one-line file per entry naming the entry's container, its parent and a fractional-index key. The logical memberInstanceIds outline and every member operation's behaviour are unchanged; storage decides only what is written. A three-way merge is per path, and its result is the decoding of the merged files. Orphans and loops left by a clean merge are warnings with a deterministic decode, re-attached by repair. Keys come from one shared algorithm. This supersedes, in part, rfc-decision-0df19d60: its accepted cost that two writers who reorder one container conflict as a whole no longer holds, since conflicts are per entry; its position, that context order is declared on the Container, stands.
fieldValues.decision_scope: How a Container is stored and merged at revision 11: the directory layout, the entry file, the decoding, the write set of each member operation, the key algorithm, the per-path merge and the migration. Does not change the logical Container, the member operations' behaviour or inputs, or how conflicts are reported (RFC-010).
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: A merge driver implementing RFC-043 [R14] as tooling only: conforming, kept as the fallback, but conflict-freedom would depend on tool configuration and GitHub's server-side merge ignores it. Per-entry files keeping depth: a clean merge can break the outline. Order kept in the head: the shared file again. Records declaring their containers: two ways to declare membership. Sharding the array: reduces conflicts rather than eliminating them. git merge=union: produces invalid JSON. A sequence CRDT or LSEQ/Logoot: site identifiers solve ties that the instanceId tie-break already makes harmless. Detached entries as fatal errors (rejected: a routine merge would leave an unloadable repository) or tombstones (rejected: a second way to remove). Writer-chosen keys (rejected: the same edit would conflict across branches).
fieldValues.accepted_costs: A breaking change at dataModelRevision 11: 101 container files holding 2,992 entries in the four first-party corpora, the four root containers, six fixture containers and two .srsj artifacts change shape, carried by a registry migration with deterministic keys; three srs scripts, one srs-vscode schema glob and one srs-web e2e test change. Any two concurrent edits to one container's head conflict, because a head is one line. A text merge can conflict where a per-path reading is clean (rename/delete, rename/rename), and three clean merges leave reported states (detached entries, a dangling pointer, a headless directory).
evidence_refs: the-greenman/srs#940 (RFC-051, accepted by the owner 2026-10-20; rulings 1-4 and seven review rounds in its comments)
rfc-decision-0df19d60 (superseded in part: its merge-cost clause)
the-greenman/clerk#91 (the bridge, and the cutover replay)
fieldValues.review_trigger: Review if detached entries (orphans, loops) are reported in more than occasional merges, which would be evidence for a merge driver or tombstones; or if container heads are edited concurrently often enough that one-line heads conflict in practice.
